runtime_expectations.reason: Both of this group's stories are UI-layer (E5-S4, E9-S4) and consume 5 endpoints already implemented and live-verified in Group G's contract (GET /api/recommendation; GET /api/advisor/customers; GET /api/advisor/customers/{id}; POST .../override; POST .../manual-recommendation — see backend/src/app/routers/recommendation.py and backend/src/app/routers/advisor.py, both confirmed present and unchanged as of this contract's authoring). Per project-manifest.json's `verification.mode: local`, the backend runs via `cd backend && uv run uvicorn src.app.main:app --host 0.0.0.0 --port 8000` — no `--reload`, matching the fix for the env-var/process-lifecycle issue Group F hit (claude-progress.txt's Group G handoff note) and which Group G's own live evaluation carried forward and re-confirmed (evaluator-report.md: "api_checks were run as real HTTP calls against the live backend (`http://localhost:8000`, uvicorn, no `--reload`)") — with `DATABASE_URL` and `JWT_SECRET` exported as real environment variables, not a `backend/.env` file (`backend/tests/unit/test_config.py::TestGitignore` asserts no such file exists on disk). The frontend runs via `cd frontend && npm run dev -- --port 5173` against that same live backend. Demo accounts share password `WealthWise-Demo-Synthetic-2026!` (see `backend/seed/demo_accounts.json` for emails/roles); the evaluator authenticates a `customer`-role account for E5-S4 checks and an `advisor`-role account for E9-S4 checks via the real login UI (`/login`), not a minted JWT injected into localStorage, so that role-based NavBar/routing is exercised honestly. The evaluator MUST start both processes and pass the `/health` probe before running playwright_checks. This group has no api_checks (see note 2) — unit_test_checks (vitest) remain a separate, additional signal and do not substitute for the live playwright_checks.

playwright_checks.description: E5-S4 AC1. The allocation view renders each asset class with its recommended percentage, and the displayed percentages sum to 100 as shown on screen.

steps.assertion: GET /api/recommendation resolves 200 and the allocation list renders, for a customer fixture with an active RiskBandAssignment
One row is rendered per entry in the response's `allocations` array, each showing its asset_class_name/code and `percent`
A displayed running/grand total is visible and reads exactly '100.00', computed by summing the rendered percentages, not merely echoing the API's `total_percent` field verbatim

playwright_checks.description: E5-S4 AC2. If the customer has no risk-band assignment, the view prompts them to complete the risk-profile questionnaire instead of showing an empty/broken chart.

steps.assertion: GET /api/recommendation resolves 404 NO_RISK_BAND_ASSIGNMENT, for a customer fixture with no RiskBandAssignment
A prompt is visible directing the customer to complete the risk-profile questionnaire; no empty table, zeroed chart, or unhandled-error state is rendered
the app navigates to /customer/questionnaire

playwright_checks.description: E5-S4 AC3. The view is reachable via a persistent navigation link from the customer dashboard.

steps.assertion: A link to /customer/allocation is visible in the persistent NavBar (rendered on every customer-role page via Layout, per the pattern established for Holdings/Goals/Rebalancing in prior groups), not only as a one-off Dashboard quick-link
the app navigates to /customer/allocation and the allocation view renders

playwright_checks.description: E5-S4 AC4. Percentage values are rendered with a consistent, fixed number of decimal places, with no floating-point rounding artifacts.

steps.assertion: the allocation list renders for a template whose lines do not divide evenly (e.g. three asset classes at 33.34/33.33/33.33)

Every rendered percentage string matches ^\d+\.\d{2}$ (exactly two decimal places); none renders a raw JS float artifact such as '33.330000000000005' or a value with a differing decimal count from its siblings

playwright_checks.description: E5-S4 AC5. The view refetches and re-renders if the customer's risk band changes (e.g., after an advisor override) without requiring a full page reload.

steps.assertion: the allocation view renders the customer's current risk_band/allocations for a customer fixture with an active RiskBandAssignment
open a second tab, log in as an advisor, drill into the same customer, and submit a valid override to a different risk band (exercises E9-S4 AC4 as the trigger)

back in the first tab, without any manual reload/navigation, a refetch (e.g. on window focus/visibility-change, a poll interval, or an app-level event) is observed and GET /api/recommendation is re-issued
The allocation view now shows the overridden risk band's allocations, and no full-page navigation/reload event fired during the update

playwright_checks.description: E9-S4 AC1. The advisor customer list screen displays every customer with their current risk band and links to a drill-in view.

steps.assertion: GET /api/advisor/customers resolves 200 and the customer list renders

The number of rendered rows equals the number of items in the response; every row shows its risk_band (or an explicit 'not assessed' treatment when null) and a link/control into that customer's drill-in view
the app navigates to that customer's drill-in route (e.g. /advisor/customers/{id}) and GET /api/advisor/customers/{id} resolves 200

playwright_checks.description: E9-S4 AC2. The drill-in view shows the customer's holdings, goals, and current allocation on a single screen.

steps.assertion: GET /api/advisor/customers/3 resolves 200 for a customer fixture with holdings, goals, and an active allocation
Holdings, goals, and current allocation sections are all visible in the same rendered page without any additional navigation/route change or tab-click to a different URL

playwright_checks.description: E9-S4 AC3. Submitting the override form without entering a reason shows an inline validation error and does not call the override API.

steps.assertion: no POST /api/advisor/customers/3/override request is issued
An inline validation error is visible next to the reason field (e.g. #reason), and the risk band shown on the drill-in view is unchanged

playwright_checks.description: E9-S4 AC4. Submitting a valid override updates the displayed risk band on the drill-in view without a full page reload.

steps.assertion: POST /api/advisor/customers/3/override resolves 201
The drill-in view's displayed risk band is now CONSERVATIVE, updated via state (no navigation/full-page reload event fired), and the override_history list includes the new entry

playwright_checks.description: E9-S4 AC5. The manual-recommendation log control is a modal/panel launched from the drill-in view, not a separate route/screen.

steps.assertion: The URL is /advisor/customers/3 before opening the control
A modal/panel (role=dialog or equivalent) is visible layered over the drill-in view, and the URL is still /advisor/customers/3 — no route change occurred

steps.value: Recommended increasing cash weighting ahead of the client's Q4 liquidity need.

steps.assertion: POST /api/advisor/customers/3/manual-recommendation resolves 201
The modal closes and the underlying drill-in view remains at /advisor/customers/3 with no new route ever having been entered

design_checks.notes: Two UI surfaces this group, scored against their own mockups (E5-S4.html, E9-S4.html) per design intent, not literal markup reuse — same convention as Group G. accessibility is kept at the standard bar (6) rather than raised, because unlike Group G's stories, neither E5-S4 nor E9-S4 carries an explicit labeling/keyboard-operability acceptance criterion this time — ordinary WCAG hygiene (label/for association, focus-visible, dialog role on the modal) still applies but is not independently AC-gated. interaction_feedback is raised to 7 (not the usual 6) because this group is dense with state-driven behavior that is fundamentally about visible feedback rather than static layout: E5-S4 AC5's live refetch-without-reload, E9-S4 AC3's inline validation, and E9-S4 AC4's in-place risk-band update. The drill-in page is listed at a concrete fixture id (/advisor/customers/3) matching the customer_id used throughout api-contracts.md §11's examples, so the evaluator has a stable, seeded target rather than needing to discover an id first.

route_registration.command: rg -n "path=./customer/allocation." frontend/src/router.tsx ; rg -n "path=./advisor/customers/:.*." frontend/src/router.tsx ; rg -n "to=./customer/allocation." frontend/src/components/NavBar.tsx ; rg -n "AdvisorCustomerListStub" frontend/src/router.tsx
route_registration.description: Explicit, non-optional deliverable flagged by the team-lead per Group G's self-heal history: frontend/src/router.tsx must register both /customer/allocation and a real dynamic /advisor/customers/:customerId drill-in route (replacing the E2-S3-era `AdvisorCustomerListStub` placeholder entirely — the last rg pattern above must return no match once this group lands), and frontend/src/components/NavBar.tsx must link to /customer/allocation from the persistent customer nav. The manual-recommendation modal must NOT register a route of its own (E9-S4 AC5) — router.tsx must show no path containing 'manual-recommendation'.

frontend_typing.description: tsc --noEmit exits 0 with zero `any` per CLAUDE.md's static-typing rule across all new/modified frontend files this group adds (Allocation.tsx, api/recommendation.ts, lib/money.ts, router.tsx, components/NavBar.tsx, pages/advisor/*.tsx, api/advisor.ts, components/Modal.tsx).

frontend_lint.description: ESLint clean on all new or modified frontend/src files this group adds.

money_ts_reuse.description: Must return no match. Allocation.tsx and CustomerDetail.tsx format every percent/money value through frontend/src/lib/money.ts's existing basis-point helpers (created by Group H's predecessor per component-map.md note 8's resolved provenance), not ad hoc `parseFloat`/`toFixed` string math — the source of the 'floating-point rounding artifacts' AC-4 explicitly forbids.

no_backend_changes.description: Must produce empty output (or, if the generator finds a genuine backend defect while wiring the UI, any change here is itself a contract deviation to flag, not a silent fix). Both of this group's stories are UI-layer per their story-file headers and consume 5 endpoints already implemented and merged in Group G; this group should touch frontend/ and specs/ only.

no_float.description: Extended scan continues to pass unchanged — this group adds no backend/domain modules; included for regression parity with every prior group's contract.

env_vars.command: cd frontend && npx detect-secrets scan src
env_vars.description: No new, unallowlisted finding across frontend/src. Backend is out of scope for this group's scan since no backend/ files are expected to change (see no_backend_changes).

unit_test_checks.assertion: Rendering Allocation.tsx with a mocked GET /api/recommendation response shows one row per allocation line, and a computed total of '100.00'.
With a mocked 404 NO_RISK_BAND_ASSIGNMENT response, Allocation.tsx renders a prompt linking to the questionnaire route instead of an empty/broken table.
NavBar renders a link to /customer/allocation for a customer-role user.
A mocked response with a non-evenly-divisible allocation set (e.g. thirds) renders every percentage with exactly two decimal places via lib/money.ts, with no raw floating-point string in the DOM.

Simulating the app's refetch trigger (e.g. a window focus/visibility event or poll tick) with a second mocked GET /api/recommendation response showing a different risk_band updates the rendered allocations via state, without unmounting/remounting the page component.
Rendering CustomerList.tsx with a mocked GET /api/advisor/customers response shows every customer's risk_band and a link/control to its drill-in route.
Rendering CustomerDetail.tsx with a mocked GET /api/advisor/customers/{id} response renders holdings, goals, and allocation sections all within the same component tree.
Submitting OverrideForm.tsx with reason left blank shows an inline validation error on the reason field and does not call the mocked override API.
Submitting OverrideForm with a mocked 201 response updates CustomerDetail's displayed risk_band via state, without a route navigation/full-page reload.

ManualRecommendationModal.tsx renders as a dialog opened from CustomerDetail.tsx's own tree (not via a router Route), and CustomerDetail.test.tsx confirms no navigation call fires when it opens or closes.

notes: 1. No feature-coverage gap found: all 10 features (F092-F096, F183-F187) already exist in features.json for this group's 2 stories, one per acceptance criterion. This contract's `features` list references them as-is; no new feature IDs were invented.

2. api_checks is intentionally empty. Both endpoint families this group's UI consumes (GET /api/recommendation; GET/POST /api/advisor/*) were already implemented in Group G and are already verified at the HTTP layer by Group G's api-g-01..api-g-10 (confirmed live in this reading of backend/src/app/routers/recommendation.py and backend/src/app/routers/advisor.py — both routers exist, call their domain services exclusively, and implement all 5 paths this group needs). Re-running the same HTTP-layer assertions here would duplicate signal without adding coverage; this group's playwright_checks instead verify the UI-layer behaviors specific to E5-S4/E9-S4 (rendering, validation, refetch-without-reload, modal-not-route) that Group G's contract explicitly deferred to this group (see sprint-contracts/G.json note 7).

3. Route-registration and nav-wiring are called out as their own architecture_check (`route_registration`), not left implicit, directly per the team-lead's instruction to avoid repeating Group G's 2-pass self-heal on this exact failure mode. It also asserts the E2-S3-era `AdvisorCustomerListStub` placeholder in router.tsx is fully replaced, since that stub is the concrete artifact this group must remove.

4. Judgment call on E5-S4 AC3 ('persistent navigation link from the customer dashboard'): read as 'reachable via the persistent NavBar that appears on every customer-role page (which is itself rendered starting from the dashboard/login redirect)', consistent with how E6-S5/E7-S5/E8-S4 each added their link to NavBar.tsx rather than only to Dashboard.tsx's one-off quick-links list (component-map.md rows for those stories all modify NavBar.tsx, not Dashboard.tsx). pw-h-03 and ut-230 test the NavBar link specifically; Dashboard.tsx is left off files_must_exist as a required edit target since AC3 does not require a Dashboard-page change, only a reachable persistent link — if the generator also updates Dashboard.tsx's quick-links for consistency with existing links there, that's a reasonable extension but not separately scored.

5. Judgment call on E5-S4 AC5's refetch trigger mechanism: the story does not mandate a specific mechanism (polling vs. window-focus vs. an app-level event bus), only the observable outcome ('refetches and re-renders ... without requiring a full page reload'). pw-h-05 tests the outcome via a two-tab scenario (real advisor override in tab 2, observed update in tab 1) rather than prescribing an implementation; ut-232 tests the same outcome at the unit level by simulating whatever trigger the generator chooses. If the generator's chosen mechanism has no observable trigger a Playwright test can drive within a reasonable wait (e.g., a very long poll interval with no focus-based fallback), that is a design choice worth flagging to the evaluator as a UX gap even if the AC is technically satisfied by a page-refresh-free background poll.

6. money.ts provenance: per sprint-contracts/G.json note 8, frontend/src/lib/money.ts was already created by Group G's E10-S4 (confirmed present on disk as frontend/src/lib/money.ts and money.test.ts). E5-S4's component-map.md row listing money.ts under 'Creates' is the same pre-existing spec/component-map inconsistency Group G already flagged for upstream correction — this contract treats it as 'Modifies/reuses' for E5-S4, consistent with Group G's resolution, and money_ts_reuse enforces that Allocation.tsx/CustomerDetail.tsx actually go through the shared helper rather than reintroducing ad hoc formatting.

7. Design-checks scope: only the two screens with a direct AC (Allocation view; advisor customer list + drill-in) are listed under `pages`. The override form and manual-recommendation modal are sub-components of the drill-in page, not separate routes (E9-S4 AC5 explicitly forbids the latter being a route), so they are exercised via playwright_checks/unit_test_checks interaction rather than as independent design_checks page entries.

8. No performance_checks: neither story introduces a new endpoint or a latency-sensitive interaction beyond what Group G's api_checks already cover; consistent with Group G's own empty performance_checks array.
